claim: Higher education in the UAE is licensed nationally by the Commission for Academic Accreditation under the Ministry of Higher Education and Scientific Research, and separately by an authority in each emirate — KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi, the Sharjah Council in Sharjah.
excerpt: Commission for Academic Accreditation is the national body responsible for ensuring the quality of higher education institutions in the UAE. It was established in 1999 under the Ministry of Higher Education. Its mandate was expanded in 2012 to include public and private higher education institutions. The commission licenses institutions and accredits their academic programmes in line with international standards. […] Knowledge and Human Development Authority (KHDA) regulates the quality of education in Dubai […] It also oversees private educational institutions and certifies higher education degrees from licensed universities in Dubai. […] Department of Education and Knowledge in Abu Dhabi (ADEK) regulates Abu Dhabi's education sector […] It oversees licensing of private institutions […]
interpretation: This is the reason the UAE is recorded as four Application Jurisdictions rather than one Destination. The government describes a licensing layer, not an admissions layer — there is no national admissions authority here at all, and the page that would name one instead names five regulators. Every institution in the country therefore runs its own admission, and what decides which rules and which calendar apply to a student is what kind of institution it is: federal, UAE private, or a foreign university's campus operating under a licence. Grouping the UAE by emirate would sort Birmingham Dubai next to Middlesex Dubai and away from Birmingham UK, which is exactly backwards.
